g3ela-32-1-teach-morph: [curious] Every word part this year was a tool. Kindness. Kind, plus ness: being kind. Joyous. Joy, plus ous: full of joy. Find the base word first, then the part. Read the words and their parts, tap See if you were right, then type the missing part of each word.
g3ela-32-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Generous. Here's my sentence. Maya gave half her lunch to a new friend; she was generous. One, read the sentence: she shared. Two, look for word parts: ous means full of. Three, check it. Generous means happy to give and share. Now fill in each sentence from the word bank, and play the matching game.
g3ela-32-1-teach-gram: [warmly] One sentence, four fixes. maya and leo goed to the library on monday. Maya and Leo are names: capitals. Monday is a day: capital M. And goed should be went. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then tap all seven words in the passage that need fixing.
g3ela-32-1-teach-spell: Front or back? Unhappy: the part un is at the front, so it's a prefix. Thankful: the part ful is at the end, so it's a suffix. Think about the questions, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words: prefix at the front, or suffix at the end.
g3ela-32-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Thoughtful. Find the ending: ful. It means full of. So thoughtful means full of kind thoughts. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-32-2-teach-vocab: Here's a good-character word that isn't in the game. Fair. Being fair means everyone plays by the same rules. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-32-2-teach-gram: Simple, compound or complex? When the bell rang, we lined up. When starts a part that can't stand alone: complex. I read, and my sister drew. Two complete thoughts joined by and: compound. Name each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the five words that are wrong.
g3ela-32-2-teach-spell: Rule detective! Which word dropped a silent e? Raking. Rake, drop the e, add i n g. Read the rule. Then read each question, and tap the one word in the row that fits.
g3ela-32-2-teach-rwm: Let's try all three parts with a different sentence, from The Tale of Despereaux. Nothing is sweeter in this sad world than the sound of someone you love calling your name. Nothing. Part one, read like a reader. The princess calls Despereaux's name, and it means everything to him. Part two, read like a writer. The author stops, then adds one more word: Nothing. The add-on makes us stop and feel it. Part three, write your own. My turn: Pizza night is the best night of the week. The best. Now it's your turn with Mrs. Lambchop's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-32-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Sad. Ness. Sadness! Being sad. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-32-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Mia said thank you and held the door. That shows blank. Courage? Hmm, not quite. Courtesy? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-32-3-teach-gram: Be the editor. my dogs bowl was empty and he looked sad. My gets a capital. Dog's gets an apostrophe: the bowl belongs to the dog. A comma goes before and. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then say the gray sentence the right way, out loud, and tap Check your sentence.
g3ela-32-3-teach-spell: Spot the mistake. She jumped in the puddel. Puddle ends in l e, so puddel is wrong. Read the rule. Each sentence has two misspelled words. Tap a word to check it, and find all six.
g3ela-32-4-teach-morph: Quick question: what does re mean? Again! Here's a word that isn't on the dice. Restart. To start again. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
g3ela-32-4-teach-vocab: Watch me connect a word to a book and to me. Loyalty. Arthur and I both show loyalty: he helps his brother Stanley get round again, and I stick by my friends. Now choose your word, and write one sentence about your character and you.
g3ela-32-4-teach-gram: Three passes, like an editor. my sisters cat runned under the bed. Pass one, capitals: My. Pass two, apostrophes: sister's. Pass three, verbs: runned should be ran. Now do your passes, and tap all seven words that need fixing.
g3ela-32-4-teach-spell: Dice roll: hiking! The base word is hike. It ended in a silent e, so the e dropped. Tap Roll the dice, say the word, and think: which rule is at work? Then tap Check my answer.
